os_version: macOS 26.5.2 (25F84), Apple Silicon, live user session
app: 16 live public websites in Chrome 151 (6 categories: vitrine, presse, commerce, media, reference, webapp, webapp-canvas)

stack_detection.method: open debug port answers /json/version; the sites themselves need no detection — the stack is the browser, not the page

channel_setup: Chrome launched detached with --remote-debugging-port=9223 --user-data-dir=<short path>, viewport normalised to 1280x800 CSS via Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride{deviceScaleFactor:1} so the pixel side is charged at CSS resolution — the CHEAPEST honest baseline for the screenshot condition. Structured side = the hardened in-page distiller (visible text + interactive elements + declared opaque regions + occlusion tagging). No login anywhere: every site is reachable logged-out.

t1_read_text.detail: 16/16 sites yielded a readable structured view on the first try, no site defeated the channel. Latency 6-46 ms per view (mean 16 ms) — two to three orders of magnitude below a screenshot round-trip. Nothing here is a lab page: Amazon.fr, Le Monde, YouTube watch, GitHub, Stripe, Excalidraw, OpenStreetMap all render through their real production stacks.

t2_enumerate.detail: Interactive elements come with boxes on every site; the number of nodes the distiller had to TAG as occluded is itself the interesting signal, because it maps onto how visually layered a site is: 0 on Hacker News (flat 1990s table layout), 5 on MDN, 12 on Wikipedia and Vercel, 47 on Apple and YouTube home, 70 on leboncoin, 79 on BBC News, 105 on Le Monde, 114 on Amazon, 142 on YouTube watch. Modern commercial pages are heavily layered and a naive DOM reader would publish ~100 clickable targets per page that are not actually hittable.

t3_live_value.detail: Not exercised here — no form was filled on third-party sites (read-only discipline). Covered by macos-chrome-cdp.

t4_living_screen.detail: Not measured per-site; the YouTube watch page is the only continuously-animating surface and it is covered by t6 as a declared opaque region.

t5_blind_action.detail: Covered in depth by the companion cell macos-web-navigation-blind-cdp (8/8 on live sites, structured view only).

t6_pictorial.detail: 7/16 sites carry canvas or video: Excalidraw (2 canvas), OpenStreetMap (its map is NOT canvas — it is tiled , so the structured view declares each tile rather than one opaque block), Apple (4 video), Stripe (2 canvas), Vercel (1 canvas), YouTube home and watch (1 video each), Amazon (1 video). Every one is emitted as a '[pixels] x,y,w,h' declaration with alt/aria-label when present. This is the fix found earlier in the campaign paying off on real pages: before it, an all-pictorial region distilled to nothing and looked like an EMPTY screen instead of an opaque one.

measurements.notes: THE HEADLINE, AND IT DEFLATES THE SYNTHETIC RESULT: averaged over 16 real sites the structured view costs 1360 tokens against 1366 for one CSS-resolution viewport screenshot — a ratio of 1.30x, not the 3.49x measured on the synthetic duel pages. The reason is structural and worth stating plainly in any paper: a screenshot has a FLAT cost that depends only on the viewport, while a structured view scales with information density. So the ratio is not a property of the method, it is a property of the page. Range 0.47x (Hacker News: 2917 tokens of pure text, the structured view costs TWICE a screenshot) to 3.11x (Vercel: 439 tokens, a sparse marketing page). By category: vitrine 2.20x, webapp-canvas 1.75x, presse 1.21x, reference 1.11x, media 0.97x, commerce 0.82x, webapp 0.80x. Structure wins on visually rich / semantically sparse pages and LOSES on text-dense ones — which is the opposite of the intuition that 'text is cheap'. Two corrections in favour of the structured side, both real: (a) a viewport screenshot only shows one screen, and covering a whole page took 7.6 screens on average (19 on Stripe and Amazon), so the whole-page comparison is 1.31x with the naive whole-document view and much better if the router only ever needs one screen; (b) at Retina 2x the screenshot costs 4784 tokens on a high-res model, moving the average ratio to 4.54x — but only 1534 on a legacy-tier model (1.46x), because the API downscales before charging. 6/16 sites raised a consent banner (Stripe, Vercel, YouTube, BBC, Amazon.fr, leboncoin), which a router must dismiss before the view means anything — it is the single most common real-web obstacle we hit, ahead of any rendering issue.

runtime_verification.method: Per-site viewport screenshot kept alongside the structured view; spot-checked visually on GitHub, DuckDuckGo and MDN against the emitted lines, plus the page-level counters (nText/nCanvas/nVideo/nImg/scrollH) read from the same DOM the distiller walked.
runtime_verification.agreement: No site produced content in the view that was absent from the screen. The declared gaps were honest ones: opaque media regions, occluded overlays, and off-viewport content dropped by design. One scope reminder carried over from macos-chrome-cdp: browser chrome (Chrome's own UI) is outside CDP's page scope and never appears in these views.

permissions_required: None (loopback CDP socket). No account, no login, no cookie import on any of the 16 sites.
